analysis.title: Monthly PPI Inflation Was 1.3%, Doubling Up on Market Expectations
key_insights: Final demand PPI rose 1.3% on the month in September 2026 and 6.3% over the year, about double what the market expected.
Goods PPI rose 2.6% in September, the largest monthly increase in BLS data going back to November 2009. Goods PPI had fallen an average of 0.3% per month since May.

Energy PPI rose 10.8% in September, above the 10.5% monthly gain in March after the start of the U.S. military conflict with Iran. Energy PPI is 35.6% above a year earlier, above the prior 2026 year-over-year high of 32.3% in May.

Core final demand PPI (ex food and energy) rose 0.7% in September versus 0.2% in August, so the jump is not only energy. PNC reads this as broader inflation having re-established roots from high energy prices and strong consumer demand.
PNC says the September PPI data point to continued upward pressure on consumer prices in coming months, with higher energy costs feeding into goods and services prices.
PNC says the report supports further Fed tightening and projects two more 25 basis point Fed Funds rate hikes through early 2027.
